title: Ardur Offline Verification Report v0.1
description: Deterministic explorer report emitted by ardur-verify after offline verification of a receipt journal or full-evidence bundle. Two boundaries a reader would otherwise get wrong. (1) `result` has no failure value: verification failures raise instead of producing a report, so the existence of a report means verification succeeded. It does not mean nothing was wrong -- the timeline may still record DENY, ERROR, and UNKNOWN governance outcomes. (2) A receipt verdict of `insufficient_evidence` appears in the timeline as the decision `ERROR`. That label reads like an operational fault but is a governance verdict meaning the evidence was lacking, not that the verifier malfunctioned.

valid.description: Always true. A report is only constructed on the success path; every failure raises OfflineVerificationError instead.

result.description: Both values are success values. `verified` is full-evidence verification; `verified_chain_only` verified the signed hash chain alone, without transparency anchors or receiver attestations.

revocation_checked.description: Required so a reader can never assume a revocation check happened by omission. The reference verifier performs no network lookup and always emits false.

trust_roots.description: Chain-only reports carry the receipt issuer alone. Full-evidence reports additionally carry the transparency log and receiver roots, which the verifier requires to be three distinct keys.

error_count.description: Count of timeline entries whose decision is ERROR, i.e. receipts with the governance verdict `insufficient_evidence`. Not a count of verifier faults.

unknown_count.description: Count of timeline entries whose decision is UNKNOWN. Required: a reader must not have to infer the absence of unknown-verdict receipts from a missing field.

anchored_count.description: Count of timeline entries with a valid anchor of any class, including the operator-administered self-hosted log. Never read this as external anchoring.

public_log_protocol_anchored_count.description: Count of timeline entries whose valid anchor's anchor_class is public-log-protocol. Necessary but not sufficient for an external-anchoring gate: the backend kind it derives from is presenter-supplied, and the log may be operator-run. A gate must additionally confirm out of band that the pinned transparency-log key belongs to a log administered outside the operator's authority.

verified_at.description: Verifier wall-clock time at which the report was produced. Not attested by any signature in the bundle.

one_time_replay_checked.description: Required so a reader can never assume a one-time-possession check happened by omission. The reference verifier never performs one and always emits false; an age bound alone does not prevent repeated presentation inside the accepted window.

receipt_id.description: Copied from the verified receipt. The identifier's own format is governed by the Execution Receipt schema, which admits more shapes than the `receipt:<hex>` form the reference proxy emits, so it is not re-constrained here.

decision.description: Display label for `verdict`: compliant -> PERMIT, violation -> DENY, insufficient_evidence -> ERROR, unknown -> UNKNOWN. ERROR is a governance verdict about missing evidence, not a verifier malfunction.

content_provenance.description: Copied verbatim from the verified receipt. Its interior is governed by the Execution Receipt v0.2 schema, not restated here.

cost_outcomes.description: Open map: the projection keeps every numeric receipt measurement whose key mentions cost, usd, or token, so the key set is not closed.

trace_id.description: Present only when the caller requested correlation fields (the telemetry export path).

arguments_hash.description: Present only when the caller requested correlation fields (the telemetry export path).

narrowing_proven.description: True only when a signed budget delta or an observed decrease proves narrowing and nothing contradicts it. A grant change alone never proves scope containment.

budget_delta.description: Copied verbatim from the verified receipt. Its interior is governed by the Execution Receipt v0.2 schema, not restated here.

budget_remaining.description: Open map keyed by budget bucket, copied from the verified receipt.

backend.description: The backend kind the anchor bundle declared, copied verbatim after the bundle verified. This value is supplied by the presenter and selects a verification branch; it is not itself signed as a statement about where the log runs. Deliberately a closed enum: a new backend must be added here, and classified under anchor_class, before the verifier can report it.

anchor_class.description: Mechanism class derived from the backend kind. The two are not symmetric. `self-hosted-log` (c2sp-local-v1) is a checked property: that backend writes a local log, so the anchor is operator-administered by construction and must never satisfy an externally-anchored gate. `public-log-protocol` (rekor-v1) means only that the public-log submission protocol was used and its evidence verified under the pinned transparency-log key; it does not establish where the log ran, because the Rekor URL accepts any HTTPS host including one inside the operator's deployment, and unlike the self-hosted branch the checkpoint origin is not pinned. Externality and independence must both be confirmed out of band by comparing trust_roots[transparency-log].spki_fingerprint and the entry's log_id against an independently trusted inventory.

transparency.description: Chain-only reports emit present/valid alone; the anchor detail keys appear only on the full-evidence path. A valid anchor MUST carry backend and anchor_class, so the contract — not just the implementation — forbids an unlabeled anchor that a reader could mistake for external anchoring.

status.description: `absent` means the report is chain-only and no receiver evidence was examined. `not-dispatched` means full evidence showed the call was blocked before dispatch.
